releases.title: Trace logs tab and multi-expression PromQL
releases.summary: The event side panel now has a "Trace logs" tab, listing a trace's logs as a flat chronological table instead of leaving you to hunt for them among the spans in the waterfall.

highlights.text: A "Trace logs" tab in the event side panel
Choose what a click on a search result does
MATERIALIZED and ALIAS columns in the row details panel
Plot several PromQL expressions on one chart
PromQL number tiles take instant queries and reductions
Sparklines behind PromQL number tiles
Table tiles on PromQL sources
Pie and bar tiles on PromQL sources
Macros in PromQL charts
Markdown tiles pick up dashboard variables
A per-source floor for auto granularity
StatsD metrics from your own collector pipeline

releases.title: Chart label clipping and image build fixes
releases.summary: This release unblocks the all-in-one and local Docker images, which copied node's entire `/usr/lib` over the ClickHouse base image and stopped building altogether once the two landed on different Alpine point releases.

releases.title: Chart alerts and required dashboard filters
releases.summary: You can now create an alert directly from a chart in the explorer, without first saving it to a dashboard tile or a saved search — build the query, add an alert, and it carries its own chart config with it.

highlights.text: PromQL against ClickHouse now goes through its Prometheus HTTP API
Alerts straight from the chart explorer
Dashboard filters can be marked required
Dashboards remember relative date ranges
Span metrics from your own collector pipeline
Filter the LLM dashboard by end user
Pick rows out of the search results table
Stored third-party tokens can be encrypted at rest
A getting-started checklist in the sidebar
Dashboard tile alerts can be exported to Terraform

releases.title: LLM observability dashboard (beta)
releases.summary: You can now see what your LLM calls cost, how many tokens they consume and how long they take to respond, without changing a line of instrumentation: a new beta dashboard at `/llm` reads the traces you have already ingested and interprets them at query time.

highlights.text: PromQL proxying keeps a Connection host's path prefix
GPU charts in the log and span side panel
Alert webhooks carry the alert's identity and condition
Inline chart alerts through the external API and MCP
Alerts carry their own display name and tags
Filters can offer a static list of values
Dashboard filters built on Prometheus label values
"Copy debug info" in the Help menu, and a window.hdx console handle
PromQL series legends can follow your own template

releases.title: Metrics explorer and in-app release notes
releases.summary: You no longer have to know a metric's name to chart it: the chart editor gains a metrics explorer that browses your metric namespace as a tree, searches every name and description the source reports, and shows a metric's kind, unit, reporting services and tag values before you commit to it.

highlights.text: Metrics explorer in the chart editor
"What's new" lives in the app
Alerts that carry their own chart, without a saved search or dashboard tile
Span links read both ways in the span detail
Dashboard variables are available to everyone
Dashboard filter values persist per variable
Exact-match Lucene variable references are distributed
Dashboard variables work in PromQL charts
Dashboard variables over the MCP server
